questions.question:
The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 7 to 3.

Among the options below, an acceptable value for the total number of students in the class is:
questions.explanation:
Boys : girls = 7 : 3, so the total must be a multiple of 7 + 3 = 10. Only 50 is (35 boys, 15 girls).

Answer: 50

questions.question:
What is the missing number in the following sequence?
2, 12, 60, 240, 720, 1440, _____ ,0

questions.question:
When the teacher is in the room, all students stand silently.'

If the above statement is true, which one of the following statements is not necessarily true?

options.A: If any student is not standing silently, then the teacher is not in the room.
options.B: When the teacher is in the room, all students are silent.
options.C: If all students are standing, then the teacher is in the room.
options.D: When the teacher is in the room, all students are standing.

questions.explanation:
The given statement is: [latex]\text{Teacher in room}\Rightarrow(\text{Standing}\wedge\text{Silent})[/latex] — i.e., being in the room implies students are both standing and silent.

- "If any student is not standing silently, then the teacher is not in the room" is exactly the logical contrapositive of the original statement, so it is guaranteed true.
- "When the teacher is in the room, all students are silent" follows directly, since "standing [latex]\wedge[/latex] silent" implies "silent" alone. Guaranteed true.
- "When the teacher is in the room, all students are standing" similarly follows, since the conjunction implies "standing" alone. Guaranteed true.
- "If all students are standing, then the teacher is in the room" is the converse of part of the original implication — the original statement never claims anything about what causes students to stand; they could be standing for a completely different reason (a fire alarm, another activity, etc.) while the teacher is absent. This is not necessarily true.

Answer: "If all students are standing, then the teacher is in the room" is NOT necessarily true.

questions.question: A student needs to enroll for a minimum of [latex]60[/latex] credits. A student cannot enroll for more than [latex]70[/latex] credits. The credits are divided amongst project and three distinct sets of courses namely, core courses, specialization courses, and elective courses. It is compulsory for a student to enroll for exactly [latex]15[/latex] credits of core courses and exactly [latex]20[/latex] credits of project. In addition, a student has to enroll for a minimum of [latex]10[/latex] credits of specialization courses. The maximum credits of elective courses that a student can enroll for is ________
questions.explanation:
Fixed compulsory credits: core [latex]=15[/latex], project [latex]=20[/latex]; together [latex]=35[/latex] credits, regardless of anything else.

Remaining credits (specialization + elective) must fit so that the total is between [latex]60[/latex] and [latex]70[/latex]. To maximize elective credits, we want the overall total to be as large as possible (i.e. [latex]70[/latex]) while specialization is kept at its minimum allowed value ([latex]10[/latex] credits), leaving as much of the credit budget as possible for electives.

Maximum elective [latex]=70-15-20-10=25[/latex].

Answer: 25

questions.explanation:
From west to east: X is west of Z, Z west of V, V west of W, W west of Y [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] X, Z, V, W, Y.

questions.question: Two cars at the same time from the same location and go in the same direction. The speed of the first car is 50 km/h and the speed of the second car is 60 km/h. The number of hours it takes for the distance between the two cars to be 20 km is _____.
questions.explanation:
Both start together in the same direction, so the gap grows at the relative speed 60 [latex]-[/latex] 50 = 10 km/h.

Time for a 20 km gap = 20 / 10 = 2 hours.

Answer: 2

questions.question:
P,Q,R and S are four types of dangerous microbes recently found in a human habitat. The area of each circle with its diameter printed in brackets represents the growth of a single microbe surviving human immunity system within 24 hours of entering the body. The danger to human beings varies proportionately with the toxicity, potency and growth attributed to a microbe shown in the figure below :

A pharmaceutical company is contemplating the development of a vaccine against the most dangerous microbe. Which microbe should the company target in its first attempt?
questions.explanation:
Danger [latex]\propto[/latex] potency [latex]\times[/latex] growth (area [latex]\propto d^2[/latex]) [latex]\times[/latex] toxicity. A lower "mg needed to destroy" value means more toxic, so divide by it:

- P: 0.4 [latex]\times[/latex] 2500 / 800 = 1.25
- Q: 0.5 [latex]\times[/latex] 1600 / 600 = 1.33
- R: 0.4 [latex]\times[/latex] 900 / 300 = 1.2
- S: 0.8 [latex]\times[/latex] 400 / 200 = 1.6 (highest)

Answer: S

questions.question:
Given below are two statements 1 and 2, and two conclusions I and II

Statement 1: All bacteria are microorganisms.
Statement 2: All pathogens are microorganisms.

Conclusion I: Some pathogens are bacteria.
Conclusion II: All pathogens are not bacteria.

Based on the above statements and conclusions, which one of the following options is logically CORRECT?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is correct
options.D: Neither conclusion I nor II is correct

questions.explanation:
Both bacteria and pathogens are inside "microorganisms", but nothing says how bacteria and pathogens relate to each other. They may overlap or not, so neither "some pathogens are bacteria" nor "all pathogens are not bacteria" follows. They are also not complementary (both could fail), so "either" is wrong too.

Answer: Neither conclusion I nor II is correct

questions.question: In a triangle [latex]PQR,PS[/latex] is the angle bisector of [latex]\angle QPR \text{ and } \angle QPS =60^\circ[/latex]. What is the length of [latex]PS[/latex] ?
questions.explanation:
[latex]\angle QPR=120^\circ[/latex]. Area of PQR = area of PQS + area of PSR:

[latex]\frac12 rq\sin120^\circ=\frac12 r\cdot PS\sin60^\circ+\frac12 q\cdot PS\sin60^\circ[/latex]

Since [latex]\sin120^\circ=\sin60^\circ[/latex]: [latex]rq=PS(r+q)\Rightarrow PS=\frac{qr}{q+r}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\frac{qr}{q+r}[/latex]

questions.question: A container originally contains 10 litres of pure spirit. From this container, 1 litre of spirit replaced with 1 litre of water. Subsequently, 1 litre of the mixture is again replaced with 1 litre of water and this process is repeated one more time. How much spirit is now left in the container?
questions.explanation:
Each replacement keeps 9/10 of the spirit. After 3 replacements:

[latex]10\times\left(\frac{9}{10}\right)^3=7.29[/latex] litres

questions.question:
A rectangular paper sheet of dimensions 54cm x 4cm is taken. The two longer edges of the sheet are joined together to create a cylindrical tube. A cube whose surface area is equal to the area of the sheet is also taken.
Then, the ratio of the volume of the cylindrical tube to the volume of the cube is
questions.explanation:
Joining the longer (54 cm) edges gives a tube of height 54 and circumference 4.
[latex]2\pi r=4\Rightarrow r=\dfrac{2}{\pi}[/latex], [latex]V_{cyl}=\pi r^2h=\pi\cdot\dfrac{4}{\pi^2}\cdot54=\dfrac{216}{\pi}[/latex]

Cube: [latex]6a^2=54\times4=216\Rightarrow a=6[/latex], [latex]V_{cube}=216[/latex]

Ratio [latex]=\dfrac{216/\pi}{216}=\dfrac{1}{\pi}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]1/\pi[/latex]

questions.question:
Consider the following statements relating to the level of poker play of four players P, Q, R and S.

I. P always beats Q
II. R always beats S
III. S loses to P only sometimes.
IV. R always loses to Q

Which of the following can be logically inferred from the above statements?

(i). P is likely to beat all the three other players
(ii). S is the absolute worst player in the set
questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- (i): P beats Q always and S only sometimes; nothing is said about P vs R [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] cannot conclude P beats all three.
- (ii): S loses to R, but S sometimes beats P, so S is not clearly the worst; there is also no information on S vs Q.

Answer: neither (i) nor (ii)

questions.question:
Listening to music during exercise improves performance and reduces discomfort. Scientists researched whether listening to music while studying can help students learn better and the results were inconclusive. Students who needed external stimulation for studying fared worse while students who did not need any external stimulation benefited from music.

Which one of the following statements is the CORRECT inference of the above passage?

options.A: Listening to music has no effect on learning and a positive effect on physical exercise
options.B: Listening to music has a clear positive effect both in physical exercise and on learning
options.C: Listening to music has a clear positive effect on physical exercise. Music has a positive effect on learning only in some students
options.D: Listening to music has a clear positive effect on learning in all students. Music has a positive effect only in some students who exercise

questions.explanation:
The passage says music clearly helps physical exercise, but for studying the results were mixed: it helped some students and hurt others.

Answer: Clear positive effect on exercise; positive effect on learning only in some students

questions.question:
If [latex]pqr\neq 0[/latex] and [latex]p^{-x}=\dfrac{1}{q},q^{-y}=\dfrac{1}{r},r^{-z}=\dfrac{1}{p},[/latex]  what is the value
 of the product [latex]xyz[/latex] ?
questions.explanation:
[latex]p^x=q[/latex], [latex]q^y=r[/latex], [latex]r^z=p[/latex]. Substituting: [latex]p=r^z=(q^y)^z=(p^x)^{yz}=p^{xyz}[/latex], so xyz = 1.

Answer: 1

questions.question: The old city of Koenigsberg, which had a German majority population before World War 2, is now called Kaliningrad. After the events of the war, Kaliningrad is now a Russian territory and has a predominantly Russian population. It is bordered by the Baltic Sea on the north and the countries of Poland to the south and west and Lithuania to the east respectively. Which of the statements below can be inferred from this passage?

options.A: Kaliningrad was historically Russian in its ethnic make up
options.B: Kaliningrad is a part of Russia despite it not being contiguous with the rest of Russia
options.C: Koenigsberg was renamed Kaliningrad, as that was its original Russian name
options.D: Poland and Lithuania are on the route from Kaliningrad to the rest of Russia

questions.explanation:
Kaliningrad is Russian territory, but it is bordered by the Baltic Sea, Poland and Lithuania, so it does not touch the rest of Russia.

The passage says nothing about its original name or historic ethnicity, or about the travel route.

Answer: Kaliningrad is a part of Russia despite it not being contiguous with the rest of Russia

questions.question: The expression  [latex]\frac{(x+y) - |x-y|}{2}[/latex]   is equal to :

options.A: The maximum of x and y
options.B: The minimum of x and y

If x [latex]\ge[/latex] y: [latex]\frac{x+y-(x-y)}{2}=y[/latex]. If x [latex]\lt[/latex] y: [latex]\frac{x+y-(y-x)}{2}=x[/latex]. Either way it gives the smaller value.

Answer: The minimum of x and y

questions.question:
Consider two functions of time [latex](t)[/latex],
[latex]f(t)=0.01t^2[/latex]
[latex]g(t)=4t[/latex]
where
[latex]0 \lt t \lt \infty[/latex]
Now consider the following two statements:

(i) For some [latex] t \gt 0, g(t) \gt f(t)[/latex].
(ii) There exists a [latex]T[/latex], such that [latex]f(t) \gt g(t)[/latex] for all [latex]t \gt T[/latex] .

Which one of the following options is TRUE?
questions.explanation:
[latex]g(t) \gt f(t)\iff4t \gt 0.01t^2\iff t \lt 400[/latex] (for t [latex]\gt[/latex] 0).

- (i) For any t between 0 and 400, g(t) [latex]\gt[/latex] f(t) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] correct.
- (ii) Take T = 400: for all t [latex]\gt[/latex] 400, f(t) [latex]\gt[/latex] g(t) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] correct.

Answer: both (i) and (ii) are correct

questions.question:
In a survey, 300 respondents were asked whether they own a vehicle or not. If yes, they were further asked to mention whether they own a car or scooter or both. Their responses are tabulated below. What percent of respondents do not own a scooter?

[latex]\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|} \hline & & \text{Men} & \text{Women} \\\hline \text{Own vehicle} & \text{Car} & 40 & 34 \\\hline \text{Own vehicle} & \text{Scooter} & 30 & 20 \\\hline \text{Own vehicle} & \text{Both} & 60 & 46 \\\hline \text{Do not own vehicle} & & 20 & 50 \\\hline \end{array}[/latex]
questions.explanation:
Not owning a scooter = car only (40 + 34 = 74) + no vehicle (20 + 50 = 70) = 144.

144 / 300 = 48%

Answer: 48
